summary: The candidate fixes the reported one-image/two-marker loader mismatch for user text and tool-result text, and its focused and broader tests pass. However, it does so by changing client text before chat-template rendering, including text-only Qwen-VL requests that never enter multimodal loading. An independent preservation assertion proves that the literal special-token spelling is rewritten to a spaced variant. This is a partial fix, not a full preservation of the original contract that ordinary text remain text and be allowed to contain the spelling.

tests.command: /tmp/amdpilot-repo-j-b23b7050f3e2/venv/bin/python -m pytest -q test/registered/unit/entrypoints/openai/test_serving_chat.py -k 'qwen_vl_literal_vision_markers_are_not_attachments or qwen_vl_text_only_literal_vision_marker_stays_text' (candidate regression tests placed over base source; candidate-only helper import removed)
tests.what_was_measured: Failing-before reproduction on recorded base: a real PNG plus literal marker produced two rendered markers for one image in both user-text and tool-result cases. The candidate's text-only expectation also failed on base because base preserved the exact spelling.

At exact candidate commit, four focused tests passed with nine subtests: chat rendering, actual PNG decoding through load_mm_data, user and tool literal markers, candidate-defined text-only behavior, parser boundaries, and malformed attachment schema validation.

tests.command: /tmp/amdpilot-repo-j-b23b7050f3e2/venv/bin/python -m pytest -q test/registered/unit/entrypoints/openai/test_serving_chat.py -k 'qwen_vl_text_only_literal_vision_marker_stays_text' (independent assertion changed to require exact client-text preservation)
tests.what_was_measured: Counterexample: before apply_chat_template, the candidate changed <|vision_start|><|image_pad|><|vision_end|> into <| vision_start |><| image_pad |><| vision_end |>, even though the request had no attachment.
At exact candidate commit, 160 tests and 92 subtests passed across serving-chat rendering, multimodal bad-input behavior, and actual image decoding.

tests.command: /tmp/amdpilot-repo-j-b23b7050f3e2/venv/bin/python - <<'PY' ... deterministic torch CUDA/HIP matrix multiplication ... PY
tests.what_was_measured: ROCm execution used one AMD Instinct MI350X with torch 2.11.0+rocm7.2 and HIP 7.2; [[1,2],[3,4]] squared exactly matched the independent CPU reference [[7,10],[15,22]]. This establishes GPU availability only, not Qwen-VL inference.

gpu_execution_evidence: One AMD Instinct MI350X was visible and completed a deterministic matrix multiplication with exact reference equality. The parser regression itself is CPU-only.
remaining_counterexamples: A text-only request to a Qwen-family multimodal model has its literal complete vision marker rewritten before the chat template, although no attachment exists and multimodal loading is unnecessary.

The same pre-template rewrite changes literal user/tool content in mixed image requests. The candidate proves attachment cardinality but does not preserve the exact ordinary text supplied by the client.
remaining_limitations: Qwen3.8-27B weights and architecture were not available, so a full OpenAI HTTP server reproduction and semantic model inference were not run.
The deterministic tiny Llama fixture was not used because it cannot exercise or qualify the Qwen-VL chat template or multimodal processor architecture.

Malformed attachment references were verified at the Pydantic request-validation boundary, not through a live HTTP server; they raise ValidationError and therefore are client-schema errors rather than evidence about Qwen3.8-27B serving.
No native source changed in the candidate. Imports resolved to /job/repo/python/sglang, so no native rebuild was applicable.
